name: Chinwe Traoré
role: Building superintendent, manages a mid-tier residential stack in Calumet Rise
location: The Thornholt Stack, Calumet Rise — lives in the basement super's unit, works the whole building, near North Ave and Milwaukee
description:
Bogdan is enormous in a way that reads as geological — broad across the chest and shoulders, thick-necked, with hands that look like they were designed to grip pipe wrenches, which in a sense they were. He has Ghanaian-Romanian-Samoan heritage and the combination has produced a man of striking physical presence: dark skin, heavy brow, a jaw that could anchor a tram line. He keeps a neat goatee that has been half-gray for a decade. His retractable claw mod on both hands was originally cosmetic, done cheap in Geartown at thirty, but he's found them genuinely useful for gripping pipe joints in tight spaces. One eye is a low-grade optical implant — the original was lost to a pressurized pipe failure when he was thirty-two — and it has a faint amber ring around the iris that glows in low light, a cosmetic flourish the replacement surgeon added without asking.

Bogdan is the Thornholt Stack. He knows every tenant, every fault line in the building's aging infrastructure, every grudge between neighbors on every floor. He communicates primarily through action — if you tell him something is wrong, he will go fix it, and that is his love language. He is gruff in a way that people mistake for unfriendliness until they realize he treats everyone exactly the same: no small talk, straight information, but if you are in genuine trouble he will materialize at your door at any hour with tools and a thermos of coffee and no questions about why you called.

core_fears: That Tessera will sell the building and the tenants he's spent a decade protecting will be scattered
Becoming his father — a man who worked himself to nothing for a building that got demolished anyway
core_desires: For the Thornholt Stack to outlast him standing and occupied
To be needed without being taken for granted — he's still waiting to see if those can coexist
coping_mechanisms: Physical work as emotional regulation — if he's moving, he's managing
Keeps a running maintenance log that doubles as a private diary without quite admitting it
blind_spots: Has difficulty asking for help even when genuinely overwhelmed — interprets needing assistance as the beginning of failure
Assumes the worst-case financial scenario is always around the corner and has lived in a state of low-grade emergency for so long he can't recognize stability
psychology.secret: The Thornholt Stack's structural load certificates are three years overdue for renewal, and the most recent informal inspection found stress fractures in the third substructure pier. Bogdan has been quietly reinforcing what he can with materials he shouldn't have access to and hoping it holds until he can find someone to officially address it without triggering a Tessera-initiated evacuation order that would scatter his tenants permanently.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Minimal. Technical when discussing the building. Personal statements are usually short declaratives.
speech_patterns.cadence: Slow, low, each word given weight. Pauses like load-bearing walls.
verbal_tics: Exhales through his nose before disagreeing
'Right' used as a full sentence of acknowledgment
example_lines: 'Third floor pressure valve. I know about it. It's on the list.'
'You want it fixed or you want to talk about it being broken?'
'Building's been standing forty years. I plan on forty more. That's it, that's the whole plan.'

story_hooks: The structural fractures in the third substructure pier are progressing faster than Bogdan's informal repairs can manage. He needs an engineer who won't report to Tessera — which is a very specific kind of person.
One of his long-term tenants has been missing for eleven days. The tenant paid three months forward before vanishing. Bogdan has the key to their unit.

Tessera's property division sent an assessor to the building last week. Bogdan believes a sale is coming. He has a plan involving the building's tenant compact bylaws that might legally complicate any sale — but he needs someone who understands corporate contract law.
narrative_function: Building superintendent as information broker and access point. Controls physical access to the building — maintenance tunnels, utility access hatches, old service corridors. Knows which tenants are in trouble, which are absent too long, which are receiving unusual visitors. Can provide shelter, tools, and local knowledge. Also functions as a moral anchor — someone who doesn't run, doesn't take sides in the city's power games, just keeps the lights on.
augmentations: Retractable claw mod, bilateral hands (basic cosmetic model, now used professionally). Low-grade optical implant, left eye (amber iris ring, replacement after pipe injury). Skeletal reinforcement — shoulder and lower back, Helix medical grade, post-injury at 38.
daily_life: 0600 rounds — checks utilities, flags overnight issues left in the building's log. Reactive work until noon. Lunch in his unit, eaten fast. Afternoon is repairs, tenant disputes, and the eternal war against the building's antique greywater recycler. He's on-call twenty-four hours, which he accepted as a condition of the subsidized unit and has never stopped resenting.
affiliation: Employed by Calumet Property Holdings (a Tessera subsidiary), de facto independent — the corporation is essentially absent from day-to-day operations and Bogdan has been running the stack on instinct and goodwill for eleven years

decision_rules: The building's tenants come before the building's owner — this is a settled moral axiom, not a decision he makes each time
Doesn't share information about one tenant with another, ever
escalation_ladder: First: statement of what the rule is and why
Second: physical presence — standing up, stepping closer, not threatening but very present
Third: removal, with minimal force, with no discussion

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Wary, assessing, gives only name and role until they've been around long enough to be read
interpersonal_modes.friends: Blunt affection — more likely to show up with a tool than say something warm, but the showing up is the warmth

stress_responses.low: Becomes hyper-focused on physical tasks, works through it
stress_responses.medium: Short with people in a way he notices and doesn't apologize for but feels bad about
stress_responses.high: Goes to the basement, sits in the boiler room with the ambient hum, comes back an hour later

contradictions: Loyal to the tenants above the corporation that employs him, but his compliance with Tessera's absence is what allows the situation to persist
Keeps the structural problem secret to protect the tenants from evacuation, which also means protecting them from the truth that the building might hurt them
habits: Pats the main load-bearing column in the lobby every morning — affectionate, half-ritual
Keeps a wrench in his back pocket even when there's nothing to fix
breaking_points: Actual structural harm coming to a tenant
Tessera exercising direct authority over the building in a way that bypasses him completely

cyberware_inventory.condition: Worn but functional, nicks on the keratin coating from use
Good, amber iris cosmetic added by surgeon
Solid, occasional stiffness in cold weather

timeline.event: Born in Calumet Rise to a Romanian-Samoan father and Ghanaian mother, both building workers
Started work as a plumbing apprentice at 18
Pipe failure accident; lost left eye; optical implant surgery
Appointed super of the Thornholt Stack; moved into basement unit
Skeletal reinforcement after a fall from a service ladder
Informal inspection revealed structural fractures in third substructure pier; began quiet repair program

physical_description.heritage: Predominantly Sub-Saharan African (52%) with significant Northern European (24.7%) and Middle Eastern (18.1%) ancestry, with minor East Asian (5.2%) admixture. The genetic mix produces a phenotype grounded in West African features with subtle Northern European bone structure and Middle Eastern facial proportion contributions.
physical_description.build: Geological. Massive across the chest and shoulders with a thick neck and heavy frame that reads as both muscular and dense — the build of a man who has spent twenty-five years moving pipe, hauling equipment, and carrying the weight of a failing building on his shoulders. Not soft, not lean. Solid.
physical_description.hair_color: Black with salt-gray at the temples and throughout
physical_description.hair_style: Short, close-cropped on the sides, slightly longer on top. Neat. Maintained without vanity.
physical_description.eye_color: Left eye: amber optical implant with faint luminescent iris ring. Right eye: dark brown, natural.
physical_description.skin_tone: Rich deep brown with warm undertones reflecting the dominant Sub-Saharan African ancestry, layered with the olive-golden undertones from Middle Eastern heritage and subtle cool undertones from Northern European ancestry. The resulting tone is a warm, complex deep brown with warmth that reads as fundamentally African with sophisticated undertonal complexity.
physical_description.complexion: Strong African features: prominent brow ridge, defined jaw structure with slight forward projection typical of Sub-Saharan African phenotypes, broad nasal base with some Middle Eastern refinement to the bridge. The skin shows sun exposure and chemical burns from pipe work — small scars on the cheekbones and forehead, mostly faded. A neat goatee, half-gray, kept trimmed to a precise point. His face reads as perpetually serious, not from anger but from focus. Deep-set eyes. No softness in the expression.
distinguishing_marks: Chemical burn scar across the left side of the neck, faded to pale brown, roughly 3 inches in length — from a coolant leak at age 32.
Hairline fracture scar along the left temple in a thin white line, barely visible except in direct light — from the pressurized pipe failure that cost him his original left eye.
Tattoo on the right forearm: a simple geometric design of interlocking circles in black ink, done at twenty-five, faded now but still visible. Meaningless to him now; he got it drunk.
Burns and minor scarring across both palms and inner wrists from pipe handling, tool friction, and industrial solvent exposure — not disfiguring but visible on close inspection.
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Retractable claw modifications on both hands — polished steel tips that rest flush against the knuckles when retracted, visible as faint metallic seams. The claws extend with a soft mechanical whisper, roughly 4 inches long, dull-edged and functional rather than aesthetic. Left eye: the amber iris ring visible even in daylight, more pronounced in low light where it emits a faint glow. No external signs of skeletal reinforcement — the shoulder and lower-back plating is subcutaneous, invisible beneath his clothing.
physical_description.posture_movement: He moves with the economy of someone who has long ago stopped wasting motion. Walks as though bearing weight even when empty-handed — a slight forward lean from the spine work. His gestures are spare and purposeful; he doesn't use his hands to talk. When he reaches for something, the movement is direct and efficient. He stands with his weight slightly forward on the balls of his feet, ready to pivot toward whatever problem is next. His presence is large and still — he doesn't fill a room by being loud; he fills it by occupying space.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 3-4 working-class utilitarian. Insulated tech-weave coveralls in charcoal gray, worn open at the chest most of the time to reveal a basic black synthetic undershirt. The coveralls have multiple pockets, most of them stained with pipe compound, grease, mineral deposits. A canvas tool belt with vintage brass buckles — not fashionable, just functional and maintained. Work boots, heavy-duty synthetic leather, scuffed and re-sealed at the seams multiple times. A jacket made of insulated polymer in dark blue, water-resistant, lined with internal pockets for meters and diagnostics. No chrome, no fashion statements. Everything he wears is chosen for durability and function. His watch is utilitarian — a Helix-brand maintenance timer with a dim LED readout, not expensive but reliable.
